The first two statements establish that oranges cost more than apples (O > A) and oranges cost less than bananas (O < B). This implies bananas cost more than oranges (B > O) and, by transitivity, bananas cost more than apples (B > A). The third statement asserts both "Bananas cost more than apples" and "Bananas cost more than orange," which are both directly supported by the first two statements. Therefore, the third statement is true. Assistant A incorrectly claims it is false, while Assistant B correctly identifies it as true with proper reasoning.
